name: The Jenkins Alley Walnut

location.address: Jenkins Alley, behind 1325 Bolton Street, Bolton Hill, Baltimore, MD 21217

official_register.name: Maryland Notable Tree Registry (per the Bolton Hill Bulletin; no per-tree page found)

access: Jenkins Alley is a back alley behind Bolton Street houses and Brown Memorial Church; no source says whether the tree is reachable on foot. View from the alley end if open; do not enter private yards.
verify_notes: One credible local source plus a state registry mention, flagged 'one source / register mention only'. Bolton Hill Bulletin July-August 2017 (vol XLVI no 7, boltonhillmd.org/?p=24225) first described it as an Eastern black walnut in Jenkins Alley shading the rear of Brown Memorial Church, trunk 'a whopping 161 inches around, which may be a record here in Bolton Hill' (161 in = about 409 cm; girth height not stated, wires from BGE run through the tree). A later Bulletin piece (boltonhillmd.org/bulletin/bolton-hills-champion-trees/) corrects the species to English walnut after Baltimore City Forestry Board volunteers Fred Chalfont and Ray Iturralde put the author right, calls it 'marvelously massive', and says it is one of two Bolton Hill trees on the Maryland Notable Tree Registry (1,750+ trees in 23 counties and Baltimore City; notable needs at least 70 percent of the state champion's points). Assumed same tree: same alley, same church context, the champion piece places it behind 1325 Bolton Street; the two articles are by the same publisher so not fully independent. Pin: building 1325 Bolton Street geocoded by Nominatim at 39.3060,-76.6246; the tree itself is in the alley behind it, not placed individually, hence approximate. Alive: lifecheck NONE; last dated evidence is the 2017 Bulletin articles, no recent observation found. Age not documented anywhere. Species caution: the 2017 black walnut label was wrong; the later correction is by the city's own forestry volunteers.
story:
The neighbourhood paper got this tree's species wrong the first time, and it took two forestry volunteers to put it right. In the summer of 2017 the Bolton Hill Bulletin described a black walnut in Jenkins Alley, shading the back of Brown Memorial Church, with a trunk "a whopping 161 inches around". That is about 4.1 metres, and the writer wondered whether it might be a record for Bolton Hill.

Then two volunteers from the Baltimore City Forestry Board set the paper straight. It is a common walnut, the Old World nut tree Americans call English walnut, not the native black. A later Bulletin piece corrected the name, called the tree "marvelously massive", and reported that it is one of two Bolton Hill trees on the Maryland Notable Tree Registry, a list of more than 1,750 trees across the state's 23 counties and Baltimore City. Making it takes 70 percent of the state champion's points.

It reached that size with BGE power lines running through its branches.

Our footing here is thin. Both articles come from the same neighbourhood publisher, the last dated word on the tree is from 2017, and nobody has published its age. Jenkins Alley runs behind the houses of Bolton Street, and we cannot tell you whether you can walk right up to the trunk. Look from the alley end, keep out of the yards, and if you have seen it standing, tell us.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the trunk, about 4.1 metres round, with BGE power lines running through its branches. It stands in Jenkins Alley behind 1325 Bolton Street, shading the back of Brown Memorial Church.
